problemStatement.formal: The Waring function g(2) = 4: every natural number is the sum of at most 4 squares, and 4 is optimal because numbers of the form 4^a(8b+7) require exactly 4 squares.
problemStatement.plain: Prove that every natural number can be written as a sum of four squares (Lagrange), that no fewer than four suffice in general (via Legendre's excluded forms), and that g(2) = 4 exactly.
whyMatters: Connects Lagrange's four-square theorem to Waring's problem
Self-contained proof of the lower bound via modular arithmetic
General descent argument showing all 4^a(8b+7) forms need 4 squares
Computable framework for analyzing square representation counts

proven: g(2) upper bound from Lagrange (Mathlib's Nat.sum_four_squares)
7 needs exactly 4 squares (g(2) lower bound witness)
All 8b+7 numbers need 4 squares (by mod 8 argument)
Descent: if n not sum of 3 squares, 4n also not (via all-even argument)
General excluded_form_needs_four: all 4^a(8b+7) need 4 squares (by induction on a)
numSquaresNeeded computable function for n=0..31 and selected values
isExcludedForm decidable classifier (9 positive, 7 negative examples)
checkExcludedMatchesFour: all excluded forms up to 100 need exactly 4 squares
Closure under 4× multiplication and k² multiplication for 3-square sums
fourth_square_essential: excluded forms truly need all 4 squares
knownResults.goal: COMPLETE - 65+ theorems proved with 0 sorries and 0 axioms

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: LagrangeFourSquaresWaringG2.lean has 442 lines with 65+ fully-proved theorems. Establishes g(2)=4 by combining Lagrange upper bound (from Mathlib) with self-contained lower bound proof via modular arithmetic. Includes general descent argument for all excluded forms 4^a(8b+7), computable numSquaresNeeded function, isExcludedForm classifier, and statistical analysis tools.
insights: The mod 8 argument is entirely self-contained - no need for Legendre's full theorem
Descent argument (4n not sum of 3 squares if n isn't) uses all-even reduction via mod 4
interval_cases + omega/decide is the reliable pattern for small modular arithmetic in Docker Mathlib
native_decide handles numSquaresNeeded computations up to ~200 efficiently
